desc: Read the input $N$ and the sorted array $A$.
Initialize two pointers: `left` pointing to the start of the array (smallest mochi) and `right` pointing to the start of the array.
If true, a valid pair is found: increment the pair count, move `left` forward, and move `right` forward to the next available mochi.

If false, the mochi at `left` is too large to be placed on top of the mochi at `right`. Since $A[\text{right}]$ is the smallest available candidate for the bottom, $A[\text{left}]$ cannot form a pair with any remaining mochi as the top element. Therefore, we must discard $A[\text{left}]$ by incrementing `left` without incrementing `right`.
Print the final count of pairs.
Ensure the solution handles constraints up to $N=5 \times 10^5$ efficiently (O(N) time complexity).
Write the Python code implementing the two-pointer greedy strategy.
Read N and the list A.
